transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, uh… I’m here because I feel like I’m always running hot. Like I can’t shut the motor off, you know? And lately it’s been getting me in trouble at the firehouse.

It’s hard to explain—like even when things are supposed to be calm, I’m still… keyed up. And at work, that doesn’t always go over well. I mean, the firehouse is already a place where everybody’s moving and talking and there’s noise, and guys are messing around, and then the tones drop—sorry, I’m kind of getting off track. But yeah, that’s the main thing. I feel like I’m constantly revved up, and it’s starting to cause problems.
Do you often feel anxious or worried?

I don’t know if I’d call it anxious, exactly. Like, I get wound up, sure, but worried… I’m not sitting there thinking, “Oh no, what if this happens?” all day or anything.

I mean, sometimes at work there’s stuff going on and my mind jumps around—like if the tones go off and someone left gear in the wrong spot, or the rig checks aren’t done right, that’ll get under my skin. Actually, last week one of the guys—sorry, that’s probably not what you’re asking. 

I guess I’m not sure. What do you mean by anxious?
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Yeah… yeah, I do. Not like I’m trying to be reckless, but my mouth gets ahead of me.

Like at the station, if the guys are talking through a plan and I already see what we should do, I’ll jump in before they’re done. I’ll cut somebody off because the answer’s already in my head, and then two seconds later I realize I just stepped on them or threw off the whole flow of the discussion.

It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I’m not trying to be a jerk. I just… I’m already there before everyone else finishes saying it.
Do you often have trouble sitting still or feel restless?

Yeah, absolutely. Sitting still is… it’s bad.

Like command meetings, when we’re all supposed to be planted in chairs and going over stuff, my body feels like it’s revving way too high. I’m sitting there thinking, okay, just stay put, listen, don’t be weird about it, but everything in me wants to get up and walk the bay, check the rigs, straighten something, do literally anything besides sit in that chair.

And then I’ll start looking around at who left what where—sorry, that’s not really the point. The point is, yeah, I feel restless a lot. Sitting still feels almost impossible sometimes.
Do you often have trouble paying attention to details or following through on instructions?

Yeah… details are a problem. I’ll think I did something right, like an incident report, and then the captain will call me over and it’s like, “You put the wrong unit number here,” or I missed a time stamp, or there’s some little box I skipped that apparently matters for the safety review.

And I swear when I finish it, I’m thinking, okay, that’s done, solid. But then it’s not. And the annoying part is it’s usually not the big story of what happened, it’s the small stuff. The little fields and numbers and times. Those are the things I keep messing up.
Do you often have intense mood swings?

Intense mood swings? I don’t know… I mean, I get irritated sometimes, but I wouldn’t know if that counts as “intense.”

Like, there are days at the firehouse where everybody’s energy is up and down anyway, depending on calls and sleep and who left dishes in the sink—sorry, that’s probably not what you’re asking.

I guess I haven’t really noticed myself swinging from one mood to another in some big way. I’d probably have to ask my wife if she sees that, because I’m not always the best judge of it.
Do you often find yourself talking more than others in social situations?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I talk a fair amount, I guess, but more than other people? Depends on who’s in the room.

At the station there are guys who can talk for an hour about one call, or a new grill, or their kid’s baseball tournament—actually one of the guys has this whole thing with travel ball, and I swear it’s like a second job for him. So compared to that, I don’t know.

My wife might say I get going sometimes, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m talking more than everybody else. I’d probably need someone else to tell me that.
Did you have any of these problems, like feeling restless or acting on impulse, when you were a kid?

Yeah, apparently I did. I don’t remember all of it super clearly, but my mom definitely does. She’ll still bring it up sometimes, like, “You were always out of your seat,” or I’d blurt out answers before the teacher finished asking.

And I guess I was losing homework a lot too, which is funny because I remember having those folders with the little Velcro flap—actually my daughter has one now, same kind of thing—and somehow stuff would still disappear. Teachers sent notes home, even though they’d say I was bright enough to do the work. It was more like I just couldn’t keep myself on track, I guess.
Did you have any periods in your childhood where you felt more in control and less restless?

I don’t really remember a stretch where I felt, like, totally in control, no. I mean, maybe some days were better than others—like if I was outside more or if the teacher was someone I liked—but my mom makes it sound like it was kind of the same pattern back in grade school.

She says I was always getting up out of my seat, blurting out answers, losing homework… and then those notes would get sent home, even though the teachers said I was smart enough to do the work. I remember some of that, but she remembers it way better than I do.
Have you experienced these feelings of restlessness and impulsivity consistently throughout your adult life as well?

Consistently through all of adulthood? I don’t know if I’d say it like that. I mean, I’ve always been kind of high-energy, I guess, especially with the job, but it really became a problem about… a year and five months ago, maybe.

That’s when the longer rotating shifts started getting piled on, and then all the extra documentation, and the drone duties got added too. The drone thing sounds cool, and it is kind of cool, but there’s a lot of paperwork and tracking and, you know, little details with it. Since all that changed, that’s when the restlessness and impulsive stuff started really getting in the way.
Have these problems, like feeling restless or acting on impulse, caused significant issues in your relationships or at work?

Yeah… at work especially. I mean, relationships too in the sense that people get annoyed, but the bigger thing is the firehouse.

It’s started costing me trust there. Like, I got pulled into this performance and safety meeting, which—sorry, I know that sounds like HR language, but in the firehouse everybody knows when something like that happens. And now I feel like my shot at moving into leadership is kind of slipping away, because the crew can’t really count on me to keep track of all the details consistently.

And that’s the part that gets to me, because I care about the job. I’m not trying to be careless. But if people start thinking, “Can we trust him with this?” that’s… yeah, that’s a big problem.
Did you have any of these problems, like feeling restless or acting on impulse, before you started working at the firehouse?

Yeah, I mean… before the firehouse, yeah, apparently it goes way back. I don’t remember all of it clearly, but my mom definitely does.

She says in grade school I was always the kid getting out of my seat, blurting answers before I was supposed to, losing homework… that kind of thing. And I’d get notes sent home, which was embarrassing because it wasn’t like I couldn’t do the work. Teachers would say I was bright enough, I just wasn’t… you know, keeping it together the way they wanted.

I guess I didn’t think of it as the same thing back then. I just thought school was boring, or I was in trouble a lot. But yeah, from what my mom says, it was there before the firehouse.
Do you think your difficulties with details and following instructions are more of a problem for you than your restlessness and impulsivity?

Yeah, I think the detail and follow-through stuff is probably the bigger problem, honestly. The restlessness is annoying, sure, but at the station it’s more like… if someone gives me three or four tasks, I’ll start off fine on the first one, and then something else grabs my attention.

Like I’ll be doing a hose inventory or an equipment checklist, and then I get pulled into another thing, or I notice something else that needs doing, and later I realize the first thing is just sitting there half-done. And then it looks like I didn’t care or wasn’t listening, which is not what I mean to do.
Have you experienced these problems at home or in other situations outside of work?

Yeah, definitely. It’s not just work.

At home I’ll forget stuff I absolutely meant to do—like paying a bill before the late fee hits, or calling somebody back. And then I’ll remember at the worst time, like when I’m driving or already in bed, and I think, “Okay, I’ll do it in a minute,” and then it’s gone again.

Even with work-related stuff outside the station, like signing off on training modules online or bringing in the right gear paperwork for my next shift… I’ll have every intention of doing it, and then I show up and realize I left it sitting on the kitchen counter. It’s frustrating because it makes me look irresponsible, but in my head I really did plan to handle it.
Are these problems you're experiencing, like forgetting things or having trouble with details, affecting your relationships with family and friends?

Yeah… I mean, with family and friends it comes up, sure, but honestly the place I feel it the most is the firehouse. Sorry, I know you asked about relationships, but that’s kind of where my closest relationships are too, in a weird way. You live with those guys on shift, you eat together, you have to trust each other.

And lately it feels like I’ve been costing myself that trust. I got pulled into this performance and safety meeting, which was… yeah, that was not a good feeling. It wasn’t like they were screaming at me, but the message was pretty clear: if I can’t keep track of details consistently, people start wondering if they can count on me.

And I’ve been wanting to move into more of a leadership role eventually, but now it feels like that’s slipping away. Like the crew sees me as someone who means well but needs to be double-checked, and that hurts.
Have you experienced these feelings of restlessness and impulsivity your entire life, or were there periods where they seemed to improve or disappear?

I don’t think it ever really disappeared, no. It’s kind of always been there in some form.

My mom will still bring up grade school stuff, actually—like she says I was always out of my seat, blurting out answers, losing homework, getting notes sent home. Which is funny because I was bright enough to do the work, so everyone would be like, “Why can’t he just sit still and turn it in?” And… yeah, I guess that sounds pretty familiar even now.
Have you experienced these feelings of restlessness and impulsivity in multiple settings, such as at home, with friends, and at work?

Yeah, at work for sure. Like sitting through command meetings… I know I’m supposed to just sit there and listen, but it feels like my body is revving too high. Like I need to stand up, walk the bay, check the rigs—just do something besides stay planted in that chair.

And it’s funny, because in the firehouse there’s always something you could be doing, you know? There’s always a compartment that could be checked or some little thing that needs fixing, and my brain kind of latches onto that instead of just… sitting still. So yeah, it’s definitely not just one place.
Have you experienced these problems with restlessness, impulsivity, and difficulty with details for more than 6 months?

Yeah, definitely more than six months. It’s been… I’d say a real problem for about a year and five months now.

It really kicked up when the longer rotating shifts started, and then they added all the extra documentation and the drone duties. The drone stuff sounds cool, and it is, but there’s a lot to keep straight, and that’s when it stopped feeling like just “oh, I’m a little scattered” and more like… okay, this is actually messing things up.
Have you noticed any periods in the past year and five months where your symptoms significantly improved or went away for a while?

Not really, no. I mean, there are maybe a good day here or there, like if the shift is quieter or I’m not buried in paperwork, but I wouldn’t say it went away.

It’s been a real problem for about… yeah, a year and five months, since they changed the rotations and then piled on the documentation and the drone duties. The drone thing kind of sounds like the fun part when you say it out loud, and sometimes it is, but it added a whole other layer of stuff to keep track of. Since then it’s been pretty steady.
Have you experienced significant problems with restlessness, impulsivity, or difficulty with details for at least 6 months prior to the last year and five months?

Yeah… I mean, if you ask my mom, she’d say this goes way back. Like grade school back.

She’s told me I was always the kid popping out of my seat, blurting out answers before the teacher finished asking, losing homework even when I’d actually done it. I got notes sent home a lot, which is funny because she always says I was plenty smart enough to do the work—I just couldn’t seem to keep myself organized or sit still long enough to not get in trouble.

I don’t know, I kind of brushed that off for years as just being a hyper kid, but yeah, it was there before this past year and a half.

doctor.question: Have you experienced these feelings of restlessness and impulsivity your entire life, or were there periods where they seemed to improve or disappear?

target_item.manifestation: My mom says I was like this back in grade school too—always out of my seat, blurting answers, losing homework, and getting notes sent home even though I was bright enough to do the work.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the restlessness and impulsivity have been present throughout life, which is most directly about childhood onset before age 12.

patient.answer:
I don’t think it ever really disappeared, no. It’s kind of always been there in some form.

My mom will still bring up grade school stuff, actually—like she says I was always out of my seat, blurting out answers, losing homework, getting notes sent home. Which is funny because I was bright enough to do the work, so everyone would be like, “Why can’t he just sit still and turn it in?” And… yeah, I guess that sounds pretty familiar even now.

doctor.intent: determine if symptoms meet criteria for persistent pattern
doctor.question: Have you experienced these feelings of restlessness and impulsivity in multiple settings, such as at home, with friends, and at work?

target_item.name: Feeling_Restless
target_item.manifestation: Sitting still through command meetings feels like my body is revving too high, like I need to stand up, walk the bay, check the rigs, do anything besides stay planted in that chair.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking most directly about restlessness across different settings, which matches the Feeling_Restless symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah, at work for sure. Like sitting through command meetings… I know I’m supposed to just sit there and listen, but it feels like my body is revving too high. Like I need to stand up, walk the bay, check the rigs—just do something besides stay planted in that chair.

And it’s funny, because in the firehouse there’s always something you could be doing, you know? There’s always a compartment that could be checked or some little thing that needs fixing, and my brain kind of latches onto that instead of just… sitting still. So yeah, it’s definitely not just one place.

doctor.intent: determine if symptoms meet criteria for persistent pattern
doctor.question: Have you experienced these problems with restlessness, impulsivity, and difficulty with details for more than 6 months?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: It’s been a real problem for about a year and five months, ever since the longer rotating shifts and extra documentation and drone duties got added.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the symptoms have been present, specifically whether they have lasted more than 6 months.

patient.answer:
Yeah, definitely more than six months. It’s been… I’d say a real problem for about a year and five months now.

It really kicked up when the longer rotating shifts started, and then they added all the extra documentation and the drone duties. The drone stuff sounds cool, and it is, but there’s a lot to keep straight, and that’s when it stopped feeling like just “oh, I’m a little scattered” and more like… okay, this is actually messing things up.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the duration criteria for a specific diagnosis
doctor.question: Have you noticed any periods in the past year and five months where your symptoms significantly improved or went away for a while?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: It’s been a real problem for about a year and five months, ever since the longer rotating shifts and extra documentation and drone duties got added.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether the symptoms persisted or remitted during the reported 1 year and 5 month duration.

patient.answer:
Not really, no. I mean, there are maybe a good day here or there, like if the shift is quieter or I’m not buried in paperwork, but I wouldn’t say it went away.

It’s been a real problem for about… yeah, a year and five months, since they changed the rotations and then piled on the documentation and the drone duties. The drone thing kind of sounds like the fun part when you say it out loud, and sometimes it is, but it added a whole other layer of stuff to keep track of. Since then it’s been pretty steady.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the duration criteria for a specific diagnosis
doctor.question: Have you experienced significant problems with restlessness, impulsivity, or difficulty with details for at least 6 months prior to the last year and five months?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: My mom says I was like this back in grade school too—always out of my seat, blurting answers, losing homework, and getting notes sent home even though I was bright enough to do the work.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether these ADHD-related problems were present before the most recent year and five months, which is most directly covered by the profile item about symptoms beginning before age 12.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, if you ask my mom, she’d say this goes way back. Like grade school back.

She’s told me I was always the kid popping out of my seat, blurting out answers before the teacher finished asking, losing homework even when I’d actually done it. I got notes sent home a lot, which is funny because she always says I was plenty smart enough to do the work—I just couldn’t seem to keep myself organized or sit still long enough to not get in trouble.

I don’t know, I kind of brushed that off for years as just being a hyper kid, but yeah, it was there before this past year and a half.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of restlessness, impulsivity, and difficulty with details have been persistent across multiple settings, including work and home, and have caused significant problems in relationships and daily life. The symptoms have been present since childhood and have continued into adulthood, meeting the criteria for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Hyperactive-Impulsive Type.
